title: Checkpoint confirm holds the state lock ~350 ms serializing a whole session record to read 8 fields
outcome: confirm_existing_checkpoint_send (engram_containment_checkpoint.rs:~719) builds its containment image without full-ledger cloning or full PersistedSessionRecord serialization under StateInner, while preserving the durable Sent-before-RPC guarantee and owner/retry checks exactly.
acceptance: Under the state lock, confirm_existing_checkpoint_send reads only the fields its containment image needs (no full PersistedSessionRecord serialization and no full-ledger clone or JSON); any ledger validation that must remain is either bounded to the checkpoint's own entries or done on an owned copy after release with the existing exact fences.

Tests show the produced containment image is byte-equal to the current implementation's image for representative sessions, that owner-change and retry-configuration refusals behave exactly as before, and that the durable Sent record still precedes the RPC.
The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding and the full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
